item.title: AI Tool Calling: Why Rust Isn't the Best Choice
item.description: After reading a 2026 Medium hit, I rebuilt the same weather CLI in five languages and re-evaluated Rust, Go, Zig, Bun, and Node.js for AI tool calling / function calling.

item.title: Go ORM Selection Notes: Is Bun Really Faster Than GORM?
item.description: A practical comparison of Bun and GORM for a SQLite sidecar project, covering performance, migration trade-offs, and writing style differences.

item.title: 11 Days, 64 AIs, 530K Lines of Code: A Complete Engineering Retrospective on Rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust
item.description: Jarred Sumner used Claude Fable 5 and 50 dynamic workflows to rewrite 535,496 lines of Zig into Rust in 11 days. An agent pipeline of 1 implementer + 2 adversarial reviewers, peaking at 1,300 lines of code per minute. This isn't 'AI helping you write code' — this is 'AI helping you make decisions.'

item.title: Reverse Engineering Claude Code's API Request Signing
item.description: An in-depth reverse engineering analysis of Claude Code's API request signing mechanism, revealing how the cch hash and xxHash64 are implemented, the secrets of Bun's runtime, and how Anthropic protects API calls with native code.

item.title: Tired of Waiting for npm install? Bun 1.3 Does It in 8 Seconds
item.description: Bun 1.3 packs a runtime, package manager, bundler, and test framework into a single executable. A large Remix project that takes npm 3 minutes 20 seconds to install? Bun does it in 8 seconds. Built-in SQL client, Redis client, zero-config frontend dev -- here's what actually changed.

item.title: Bun (Elysia) vs Rust (Actix) Performance Showdown: A Real-World Benchmark
item.description: Which is faster, Bun or Rust? This article uses a real-world URL shortener service benchmark to compare Bun (Elysia) and Rust (Actix) in throughput, latency, and developer experience, helping you choose the right tech stack.
